incident-bot: :rotating_light: DETECTED: service /v1/generate p50/p95 latency regression in hosted-us-west (observed at 02:46 UTC). Thread root ts 2409998888
ops-oncall: paging @maria @ajay @devon @tara — alert fired at 02:46. Symptoms: p50 ~90ms -> 240ms, p95 ~420ms -> 1.9s, increased tail timeouts at edge. No significant error-rate increase (5xx ~ baseline).
maria: oncall ack. devon, grab distributed traces and model-worker logs. ajay, check infra (kernel, firmware, NVMe driver). tara, scope customer impact and any support tickets.
devon: pulling traces (tempo). Initial look: long kernel-io and sched wait spans on affected traces. I’m seeing a pattern where requests hitting cold KV cache result in kernel wait spikes. Sample trace snippet:
```
trace=0xabc123 span:/infer -> 180ms
 span:kv-lookup -> 14ms
 span:kernel-wait -> 120ms
 span:gpu-exec -> 28ms
 total -> 262ms
```
ajay: infra FYI — auto-roll of kernel 6.3.1 landed in gpu-pool at 02:40 UTC (staggered). Also saw firmware update on nvme controller rolled at 02:38 but that was to a subset of nodes. I'll fetch hosts list.
ops-oncall: timeline so far: 02:38 fw-roll nvme subset, 02:40 kernel auto-roll start, 02:46 p95 spike and alert.
maria: hypotheses: (A) kernel/firmware change affecting NVMe completion latency; (B) GC/eviction causing more cold reads; (C) scheduler change in kernel causing increased syscall blocking. Assign owners: ajay -> hypothesis A, devon -> B, tara -> C (edge/batching).
-- HYPOTHESES --
A) NVMe FW/driver regression (ajay) [checking SMART & controller logs]
B) KV eviction causing disk reads (devon) [gathering cache hit-rate traces]
C) scheduler syscalls increased under new kernel (tara) [ingress/batching metrics]

tara: ingress metrics show a brief surge of concurrent large-batch client uploads at 02:35-02:42 UTC (increased batch concurrency ~2.3x). Could amplify queueing.
devon: node logs show NVMe completion latencies spiking on nodes that had firmware update:
```
[02:44:11] nvme0.0: completion q0 150ms
[02:45:02] model-worker-03 kernel: schedule_wait 95ms
[02:45:10] model-worker-09 nvme: io completion 210ms
```
ajay: cross-checking host list — nodes with firmware update overlap with nodes running kernel 6.3.1 for batch-2. Looks like two correlated changes.
ops-oncall: mitigation options — we can: 1) roll back kernel on a canary subset; 2) pin NVMe firmware back to previous; 3) enable kv-cache sticky; 4) apply edge throttle for large-batch clients. We should run in parallel small experiments.
maria: do them in parallel. ajay start kernel revert on 3 nodes (canary). devon toggle kv-cache sticky for hosted-us-west. tara apply temporary rate-limit for large-batch endpoints.
ajay: running revert on canary set (gpu-canary-1..3) with ansible at 02:58 UTC:
```
ansible-playbook -i inventory revert-kernel.yml --limit gpu-canary-1,gpu-canary-2,gpu-canary-3
```
Started.
devon: toggled kv-cache sticky at 02:59 UTC. Within 60s NVMe read rate for hosted-us-west decreased ~65%. Traces for sticky requests show kernel wait spans reduced.
tara: edge throttle active at 02:59:30 UTC — large-batch concurrency trimmed down to baseline. Some clients with heavy batching reported shorter tail times.
ops-oncall: rerouted 10% traffic to dedicated-us-west around 03:01 UTC for extra capacity. That reduced 504s.

ajay: canary revert completed at 03:06 UTC. Observed p95 on canary nodes fall from ~1.9s -> ~520ms. Good signal but not fully baseline.

devon: after sticky toggle, overall NVMe reads down, and cache-hit for token hotsets improved. But some traces still show kernel-wait spikes on nodes that had firmware update. Likely both kernel and firmware involved.
ajay: starting firmware rollback on the subset that got firmware 2.4.7 -> rolling back to 2.4.5 (controller fw) on 2 nodes at 03:12 UTC for test. Command:
```
nvme-fw-recover --device /dev/nvme0 --fw 2.4.5
```

maria: quick perf sample from affected host (03:00-03:04 window) from `perf stat`:
```
cycles: 900M
instructions: 310M
context-switches: 4200/s (baseline 100/s)
cpu-migrations: 300/s
```
High context-switch and cpu-migrations correlate with kernel wait.

ops-oncall: update: after kernel revert + kv sticky + throttle, cluster p95 improved from 1.9s -> ~450-600ms cluster-wide by 03:15 UTC. Some nodes still showing elevated tail. Severity lowered to sev3, monitoring.

devon: collecting artifacts for RCA: pre/post histograms, 20 sample traces, KV cache metrics, node iostat and nvme controller logs.
ajay: will run kernel bisect in staging to isolate commit and file to distro team. Also opening bug with storage vendor for firmware regression.

maria: interim conclusion: combined regression from (1) NVMe firmware change that increased io completion latency on a subset of controllers, and (2) kernel scheduling changes that amplify syscall blocking under our high concurrency short-syscall workload. KV cache misses and increased client batch concurrency amplified visible customer impact.

pm-oliver: customer comms queued: "We saw a latency regression in US-West caused by a recent platform firmware/kernel rollout. We reverted the kernel on canaries and toggled cache behavior; a full rollback and firmware remediation are in progress. We'll follow with a detailed postmortem."

ops-oncall: handoff to SRE team at 03:30 UTC. I will stay on rotation until full remediation.

maria: RCA action items (owners):
- ajay: collect kernel change list, reproduce in staging with workload replay, run bisect, open distro bug.
- devon: attach traces + histograms pre/post revert, KV metrics, sample logs (nvme controller).
- tara: edge telemetry showing batch concurrency and rate-limit impact, propose runbook update (hold auto-rolls for gpu-pool until staged tests).
- ops-oncall: timeline + revert logs + routing changes.

devon: preliminary numbers for postmortem: pre-mitigation p95 1.9s, post-mitigation cluster p95 ~520ms, canary nodes ~480ms. 12 tenants experienced >1s p95, 3 tenants saw 504s.

maria: marking hypotheses status: A) NVMe firmware regression -> supported (controller logs + read latency); B) KV eviction amplified -> supported (kv sticky lowered NVMe reads); C) kernel scheduler change -> supported (context-switch spike and improvement on kernel revert). Root cause is multi-factor.

pm-oliver: will prepare customer-facing timeline and notify account teams.
maria: thank you everyone. I'll write the postmortem and link artifacts here. Incident resolved -> mitigation in place, monitoring. severity downgraded. incident-bot: Incident closed/archived. Duration 02:46-03:30 UTC. :white_check_mark:
